extracted.intended_audience: immigration practitioners, stakeholders, and public commenters on the DHS proposed rule
extracted.subtask_description: Economic-analysis section of DHS's proposed public-charge rule describing assumptions, per-form time burdens, fee amounts, population estimates, and cost calculations for immigration forms and supporting documentation (I-485, I-693, I-912, I-864 family sponsor forms, I-129 series, I-539, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of GSA POV mileage reimbursement rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Uses the U.S. General Services Administration’s (GSA) travel rate of $0.545 per mile to estimate travel costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS assumes each applicant would travel independently to an ASC to submit biometrics; calculation shown (Biometrics collection travel costs * Estimated annual population) yields $27.25 per applicant and $10,416,694 total annual travel cost for biometrics collection for Form I-485.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assume each applicant travels independently to ASC
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS assumes that each applicant would travel independently to an ASC to submit his or her biometrics, meaning the rule would impose a travel cost on each applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This assumption underlies the travel cost calculation for biometrics collection and uses the GSA mileage reimbursement rate to derive per-applicant travel cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total current annual cost for filing Form I-485
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS estimates the total current annual cost for filing Form I-485 is $519,114,512.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This total includes Form I-485 filing fees, biometrics services fees, opportunity cost of time for completing Form I-485 and submitting biometrics information, and travel cost associated with biometrics collection. Detailed component calculations are shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical examination requirement (Form I-693)
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS requires most applicants who file Form I-485 to submit Form I-693 completed by a designated civil surgeon; the medical examination is required to establish that an applicant is not inadmissible on health-related grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS reiterates that these are costs applicants currently incur, not additional costs from the proposed rule. Applicants pay all medical exam costs directly to providers; USCIS does not regulate civil surgeon fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical exam fee range and average cost
rubrics_metrics.description: Medical examination fees may vary widely, from as little as $20 to as much as $1,000 per respondent (including vaccinations and additional evaluations); DHS estimates the average cost is $490 and assumes all applicants incur this cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Source cited: PRA Supporting Statement for Form I-693. Using the average and the estimated annual population (382,264) yields $187,309,360 annual medical exam costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form I-693 time burden estimate
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS estimates the time burden associated with filing Form I-693 is 2.5 hours per applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes understanding/completing the form, setting an appointment, sitting for the exam, understanding results, allowing the civil surgeon to report results, and submitting the report to USCIS. Using $10.66/hr yields an opportunity cost of $26.65 per applicant and $10,187,336 annually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postage cost per Form I-693 package
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS estimates each applicant will incur an estimated average cost of $3.75 in postage to submit the completed Form I-693 package to USCIS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using the population estimate (382,264) yields $1,433,490 annual postage cost. Source: PRA Supporting Statement for Form I-693.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total current annual cost for filing Form I-693
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS estimates the total current annual cost for filing Form I-693 is $198,930,186.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Total comprises medical exam costs ($187,309,360), opportunity cost of time for Form I-693 ($10,187,336), and postage costs ($1,433,490).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of approved Form I-912 (fee waiver)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant’s Form I-912 is approved, USCIS will waive both the filing fee and biometric services fee for an application or petition (e.g., I-485).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS assumes waived fees for analyses where an approved I-912 accompanies I-485. Filing Form I-912 is not required for applications/petitions without a filing fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimated population requesting fee waiver (Form I-912)
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on FY2012–2016 receipts, estimated average annual population requesting a fee waiver for Form I-485 is 58,558.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table data provided (receipts/approvals/denials) and DHS notes inability to determine visa-class-specific fee waiver counts for those subject to public-charge review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form I-912 time burden and opportunity cost
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS estimates the time burden for filing Form I-912 is 1 hour and 10 minutes (1.17 hours) per applicant, including instruction review, gathering documentation, completing the request, preparing statements, and submitting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using $10.66/hr gives an opportunity cost of $12.47 per applicant and $730,218 annually for the estimated population of 58,558.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form I-912 postage cost
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS estimates each applicant will incur $3.75 in postage to submit Form I-912; annual postage for 58,558 requests is $219,593.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combined with opportunity cost yields total current annual cost for I-912 of $949,811 (opportunity cost + postage).

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit of Support requirement (Form I-864 family sponsor forms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitting an affidavit of support using Form I-864 is required for most family-based immigrants and some employment-based immigrants to show adequate means of financial support (not likely to become a public charge).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form I-864 may be accompanied by I-864A (household member contract) or I-864EZ (if criteria met). Certain classes file I-864W (exempt) but DHS proposes to eliminate I-864W and require that information be provided on Form I-485.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form I-864 time burden and valuation
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS estimates the time burden for a sponsor filing Form I-864 is 6 hours per petitioner (reviewing instructions, gathering documentation, completing affidavit, preparing attachments, submitting).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using an average total rate of compensation of $35.78/hr produces an opportunity cost of $214.68 per petitioner; with estimated annual population 257,610, annual opportunity cost is $55,303,715 (taken as total current annual cost for filing I-864).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form I-864A, I-864EZ, I-864W time burdens and valuations
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS estimates I-864A takes 1.75 hours ($62.62 at $35.78/hr), I-864EZ takes 2.5 hours ($89.45 at $35.78/hr), and I-864W takes 1 hour ($35.78).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS notes inability to determine number of I-864A/I-864EZ/I-864W filings precisely and relies on I-864 annual cost estimates; proposed elimination of I-864W would shift its information collection to I-485.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed amendment to Form I-864P (HHS Poverty Guidelines)
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS proposes to amend the HHS Poverty Guidelines for Affidavit of Support (Form I-864P) by removing certain language describing means-tested public benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS states it does not anticipate additional costs or benefits resulting from proposed changes to Form I-864P.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for nonimmigrants seeking extension/change of status regarding public benefits (proposed 212.21(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule seeks to require nonimmigrants seeking extension of stay or change of status to demonstrate they have not previously received, are not currently receiving, nor are likely to receive public benefits as defined in 8 CFR 212.21(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS notes costs in this section are costs petitioners/applicants currently incur as part of requesting an extension/change of status, not additional costs from the proposed rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form I-129 filing fee and estimated annual cost
rubrics_metrics.description: The current filing fee for Form I-129 is $460.00; using estimated average annual population of employers filing on behalf of nonimmigrant workers seeking EOS/COS of 336,335, DHS estimates annual cost associated with filing Form I-129 is approximately $154,714,100.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee level set to recover DHS processing costs; detailed population assumptions provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form I-129 time burden and opportunity cost
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS estimates the time burden for completing Form I-129 is 2 hours and 20 minutes (2.34 hours).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using the average total rate of compensation of $35.78/hr yields opportunity cost of $83.73 per petitioner and $28,161,330 annually for 336,335 filings; postage of $3.75 per filing yields $1,261,256 annual postage; total current annual cost for I-129 is $184,136,686 (fees + opportunity cost + postage).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form I-129CW fees and costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Form I-129CW fee is $460 plus a $200 supplemental CNMI education fee and $50 fraud prevention and detection fee, totaling $710 per beneficiary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimated annual population filing I-129CW is 6,307; annual fee cost $4,477,970. Time burden estimated at 3.0 hours (opportunity cost $107.34 at $35.78/hr), yielding $676,993 annual opportunity cost; total current annual cost estimated $5,154,963.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form I-539 filing fee, time burden, and total annual cost
rubrics_metrics.description: The current filing fee for Form I-539 is $370; estimated average annual population seeking EOS/COS using Form I-539 is 174,866, yielding annual fee cost $64,700,420.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time burden estimated at 1.88 hours; using $35.78/hr yields opportunity cost $67.27 per applicant and $11,763,236 annually; total current annual cost for I-539 is $76,463,656 (fees + opportunity cost).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of different wage rates for opportunity cost valuation
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS uses $10.66 per hour (federal minimum wage with upward adjustment for benefits) as the total rate of compensation to value time for applicants requesting fee waivers and many applicants; DHS uses $35.78 per hour average total rate of compensation to value time for sponsors, petitioners, and certain other filers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS explains choice: fee waiver requesters are expected to hold lower-wage occupations; sponsors/petitioners are expected to have higher average compensation, justifying higher valuation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postage cost assumption per USCIS package
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS consistently estimates $3.75 average postage cost per applicant/package to submit completed form packages to USCIS (applied to Forms I-693, I-912, I-129, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied across multiple form annual cost calculations to derive annual postage totals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Framing of examined costs as 'current' not rule-imposed
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS repeatedly notes that costs examined in these sections are not additional costs imposed by the proposed rule, but costs that applicants/petitioners currently would incur as part of application processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This framing affects interpretation of which costs are attributable to the proposed regulatory change versus baseline compliance costs.
